title: A poster, a second place, and a lot of hallway talk

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Picture a congress hall full of student researchers, and one poster about how a texture wears out in real time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Texture wear? Like a virtual sneaker getting scuffed?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something like that. Antoine presented a poster at CAÉC 2026, the annual congress of student researchers. It was about simulating the visual wear of textures in real time, fed by experimental data.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the wear isn't just invented by an artist. It comes from measurements.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the idea on the page. The data is experimental, and the simulation runs in real time. And it paid off: he placed second in the Optics category.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. What did people actually ask him about at the poster?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The conversations went in a few directions: automatic commit classification, training models with other models, and optics. He also talked with Samuel Lefebvre about virtual reality interaction, and what makes a virtual world feel more credible.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a fun range for one poster.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is. The closing ceremony was hosted by Leyla Agosti Cagalli Burri, and the LinkedIn post links a paper related to work shown at the congress.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is this connected to his thesis?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. The thesis write-up is a separate article on wear in texture space, and this post links to it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the poster is the conference-hall version of that work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's a fair way to put it. Second place in Optics, and some good conversations about making virtual surfaces believable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If you want the thesis side of the story, the written page points you straight to that article.
